title: Tokens and permissions
summary: Choose Token-2022 extensions at initialization and treat permissioned-token controls as security- and compliance-sensitive program logic.

links.description: Choose Token-2022 mint and account features from the official extension map. Most extensions must be selected during initialization, and some combinations are incompatible.

Implement sRFC37 permissioned transfers with the Token ACL program and pluggable gates. Its ABL gate is a reference implementation; production use requires security audits, key management, regulatory review, and legal consultation.

title: Payments + Commerce
summary: Accept payments and build commerce on Solana.

links.description: Implement repeated payments with off-chain signed updates and onchain open and settle transactions. Treat current benchmark and partner claims as launch data, not guarantees.

Use Solana's shared subscriptions program for fixed or recurring delegation with documented program IDs and audit history. Pullers can transfer within an active authorization, so users and applications must enforce caps, expiry, revocation, and token-account delegation.

Design production payment ingestion with persistent streaming, historical access, and instruction parsing when RPC polling is not enough. The guide uses provider-backed gRPC and raw decoding, so plan the supporting infrastructure.
The Swig repository was updated 2026-08-18 and contains separate Kit and classic web3.js packages and examples. It is an active protocol SDK, not a general Solana TypeScript client.

The live portal is an authenticated Swig developer surface. Its public shell verifies the destination, but provisioning and post-login behavior could not be inspected without an account; list it only beside the public Swig docs.

title: DeFi + Stablecoins
summary: Build with interest-bearing dollars and stablecoin primitives.

links.description: Integrate Reflect's Solana protocol and SDK only when its asset and smart contract risks fit the product.
@reflectmoney/stable.ts 5.3.2 has Kit examples and migration guidance for Reflect-specific integrations. Pin the selected version.
Phantom's current docs describe CASH and its developer workflow. Development access and minting constraints make it a vendor-specific payment path rather than a default stablecoin primitive.
Use LI.FI for cross-chain Solana routing, with the documented single-step route limitation. It is an optional bridge layer, not core Solana infrastructure.

title: Blinks + Actions
summary: Build shareable transaction interfaces for any Solana action.

links.description: Dialect's implementation repository was active in August 2026. Its Solana packages still expose web3.js/wallet-adapter integration, so it is useful for Blinks specifically but not the default client scaffold.
Dialect maintains the Blinks client and integration documentation. Current install examples still use web3.js v1 and wallet-adapter, so new Kit applications need an explicit compatibility boundary.
@solana/actions 1.6.6 depends on web3.js v1. Pin it and isolate the feature-specific integration from a Kit-first client.

title: Mobile
summary: Build native mobile apps powered by Solana.

links.description: The 2026-04-27 snapshot uses Phantom React Native SDK 2.0.2, Expo 54, React Native 0.81.5, and web3.js v1; it requires a custom development build rather than Expo Go. No repository license is declared.

title: Games
summary: Build fully on-chain games or integrate Solana into existing engines.

links.description: The MIT-licensed Unity SDK was updated 2026-09-12. It is the strongest current engine-specific source in the list, but teams should pin a release/commit and test wallet support on target platforms.
Use the Rust engine documentation as a specialized community game path. Pin the engine and Solana integration versions.

The MIT-licensed Godot SDK was committed in April 2026 and includes examples. It is community-maintained and engine-specific, so pin a commit and verify RPC, wallet, and transaction compatibility before adopting it.
The official examples cover inspectable game patterns, but some samples include legacy Anchor links or Clockwork. Inspect each manifest and pin current dependencies before copying code.
This is Solana's 2023 bootcamp episode 1, published 2023-07-25. Keep for structured conceptual instruction, but do not copy dependency or CLI commands without checking current docs.
The official 'Tutorial: Building Games on Solana' was published 2023-07-03. Keep as game architecture orientation, with current examples/docs used for implementation.
The official energy-system game tutorial was published 2023-04-21. It covers a distinct design pattern, but builders must modernize dependencies and security assumptions.

The official session-key game tutorial was published 2023-05-11 and covers a still-relevant UX/security tradeoff. Use it conceptually and validate any delegated authority design against current wallet and program tooling.
The official large-account game tutorial was published 2023-03-30. The account-sizing problem remains relevant, but current framework syntax and limits must come from maintained docs.
Superteam Germany's September 2023 Solana gaming workshop. Treat package, framework, and tooling instructions as dated.

title: Agents + Tokenization
summary: Build AI agents with onchain identity and economic functionality.

links.description: The official skills index includes Foundation-maintained skills and labels community contributions separately. It reinforces the current Kit and LiteSVM/Mollusk/Surfpool testing path; community skills are not Solana endorsements.
Use the SOL and USDC balance and transfer workflows on Solana. Trading and onchain query coverage is narrower or EVM-specific.
The current x402 overview explicitly documents Solana alongside Base. Keep as protocol/vendor context, then use Solana's own x402 guide for chain-specific implementation.
Use Solana's chain-specific x402 guide for agent payments. The Coinbase buyer MCP path that this replaces is EVM-oriented.
Use the Solana Foundation CLI to access x402 or MPP services while a local wallet authorizes each payment. Review each request and keep wallet policy explicit.

The repository was updated 2026-06-10 and explicitly covers Solana among many chains. Keep only for cross-chain agent routing; it returns workflows/transactions that still require wallet policy and validation.

The live MCP docs cover route discovery and unsigned transaction construction across Solana and other chains. The public service is rate-limited and does not remove wallet signing or transaction validation responsibilities.
This Solana transaction API requires onboarding and an API key. Its latency, routing, compliance, and security claims are vendor claims, not independent benchmarks.

The live catalog exposes paid, x402-discoverable services and includes Solana among its network labels. Keep only as an optional discovery directory: listings, capability claims, and prices are provider-supplied and can change independently of the catalog.
Use Metaplex's Umi-based Agent Kit for agent and NFT workflows. This is a specialized integration, not core Kit guidance.
Register an agent through Metaplex's onchain registry. This product workflow is optional, not a requirement for general Solana agents.
Connect a runtime and fund its Metaplex registry wallet. Treat this as a specialized Metaplex integration.

The current Metaplex guide provides a concrete agent-token workflow. Token issuance introduces authority, metadata, market, and financial risks and should never be presented as a routine prerequisite.

Metaplex maintains the agent skill documentation for its own SDK and registry flows. It is a product-specific automation surface; users should review transactions and versions rather than grant unattended authority by default.
Browse Metaplex registry entries, but do not treat provider-supplied agent and token metadata as independent security endorsements.
Use Metaplex's current portal for tokenization and digital asset APIs.
The maintained Swig documentation covers its Solana smart-wallet protocol, permissions, SDKs, and integrations. It is a specialized account-control choice, not a default wallet prerequisite.

The tutorial provides an executable Swig TypeScript workflow. The current swig-ts repository separates Kit and classic web3.js packages, so builders must select the matching client rather than mix examples blindly.

title: Privacy + Confidential Compute
summary: Build encrypted applications with private state and secure computation.

links.description: Arcium's maintained documentation explains its encrypted-computation network and Solana integration. The technology adds a distinct compiler, network, and threat model and is optional for apps that truly require confidential computation.

This developer section supplies the actionable Arcis and Anchor-compatible build path, distinct from the conceptual docs home. Builders still need to validate network availability and security assumptions for their use case.

Hide transfer amounts and confidential balances with Token-2022 confidential transfers. Addresses, mints, and owners remain public; both accounts need the extension, stock solana-test-validator lacks the proof program, transfers may require several transactions, and Rust and JavaScript clients differ.

title: Governance / DAOs
summary: Build governance and DAO tooling on Solana.

links.description: The live Solana governance application remains available. It is useful as a product/protocol destination, while implementers should follow its linked SDK/program sources for versioned developer work.
MetaDAO maintains product and protocol documentation for its Solana governance and market mechanisms. Keep as a specialized integration/reference, not a general governance default.

title: Treasury + Security
summary: Secure assets, manage treasuries, and run financial operations.

links.description: The live product is backed by the public Squads v4 repository, updated 2026-08-20. Its SDK uses web3.js v1 while the program uses Anchor 0.32, making it useful production evidence with an explicit legacy boundary.
